target_customer: Used car dealers in Nigeria and Africa, plus agent dealers and global vehicle suppliers
problem: African car dealers struggle to source, finance and sell vehicles with informal operations and costly credit. Shekel offers a marketplace, dealer credit and management tools.
business_model: B2B marketplace with dealer financing and trade fees, partnering with licensed institutions for credit

founders.name: Sanmi Olukanmi
previous_startups: Founded and exited automotive enterprises averaging about $900K ARR (not named)
founders.background_notes: About 10 years in the automotive industry per YC page.

founders.name: Benjamen Oladokun
founders.background_notes: Led teams that launched mobility products in sub-Saharan Africa per YC page. Role CBO per a search result.

founders.name: Valentine Mayaki
founders.background_notes: 10+ years building fintech applications per YC page.

competitors.name: Autochek
competitors.what: Car marketplace and financing platform in Nigeria, founded by an ex Cars45 executive

competitors.name: Cars45
competitors.what: Used car marketplace with vehicle inspection and instalment financing

technical_complexity.rationale: Dealer platform, credit decisioning with licensed lenders and cross border trade logistics, with the company later citing SOC 2 Type I security work.

defensibility.rationale: Dealer credit and inventory records tie dealers to the platform and supplier plus dealer sides create a network, but competitors like Autochek were already funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Shekel through 2026. Competitors continued to run financing and marketplace models, per a March 2024 TechCabal report on inflation pressure in auto finance.

market_need_then: The company cites a $30B African used car market. Nigerian bank car loans carried 18 to 30 percent annual rates per a 2021 TechCabal report, and dealers used informal trading without financing tools.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, aspirational and pan African, with tagline Join Africa's auto trade movement

branding.brand_signature: Staff call themselves the Sheyks per the careers page
branding.community_and_virality: Dealer testimonials and press in Nigerian tech outlets; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name suggests money and is memorable, and press covered the funding widely, but no source shows brand driven growth. Shekel is also an Israeli currency name, which may confuse.

outcome_analysis: Shekel Mobility raised a $1.95M pre-seed in January 2023 and about $7M in November 2023, roughly $3.2M equity and over $4M debt, then reported about $2M ARR and plans for a priced round. Its site now claims 1,000 dealers and $50 million in powered transactions. Founders with long automotive experience and credit linked products fit a large market, though growth claims are self reported and no later round was found.
notes: The November 2023 round is reported as over $7M in total, split into $3.2M equity and over $4M debt, so it is recorded as a seed and a debt entry; the split of investors between the two is approximate. Pre-seed was cross-checked across several outlets; seed by Nairametrics, Techpoint and others. Aggregators list totals of $9.2M to $12.2M that likely double count. An undated AFROTECH article may describe the same round or a later one, so later rounds could be missing, hence partial coverage. Founded 2021 or 2022 depending on source. CBO role for Oladokun and surname for Valentine Mayaki come from secondary profiles, YC page gives names only.
